article.title: Israeli forces raid Al-Ama’ri Refugee Camp, detain dozens of Palestinians
article.author: Aseel Saleh
article.content: On Monday, November 23, the Israeli military stormed Al-Ama’ri refugee camp in Al-Bireh city in the central occupied West Bank. During the hours-long raid, Israeli forces converted the Al-Ama’ri Youth Center, alongside several residential homes, into temporary detention and field interrogation sites. They also damaged the facilities of the center. 30 Palestinians were briefly detained and interrogated after their homes were raided, but were released before the military left the camp. However, one Palestinian young man was arrested in the assault, during which stun grenades and tear gas were fired. Since January 2025, the Israeli military has intensified its campaigns against refugee camps across the West Bank, considering them bases for resistance groups in the occupied territory. These campaigns resulted in 102 fatalities , including 21 children. They also displaced over 34,000 Palestine refugees, among them 12,000 children, from Jenin, Tulkarm, and Nur Shams refugee camps. Furthermore, the Israeli army issued demolition orders for 514 buildings, according to a report published by the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) in September, 2026. On November 17, 2026, Israeli authorities issued order No. 123/26 , authorizing the seizure of neighborhoods and road networks in Tulkarm and the nearby neighborhood of Dhannaba for “military purposes.” The order, which encompasses Tulkarm Refugee Camp, is valid until December 31, 2028, raising acute concerns that Israel intends to permanently displace the residents, who fled the camp as a result of the previous military campaign.
